hook.text: The human genome compresses from 800 MB to about 4 MB with standard algorithms. That reveals extreme redundancy.

buildup.text: Repetitive sequences, palindromes, and tandem repeats create massive redundancy that compressors exploit.

discovery.text: About 45% of the human genome consists of transposable elements—sequences that copy-pasted themselves throughout.

twist.text: Species with larger genomes often have more repetitive DNA, not more genes. Size reflects redundancy, not complexity.

climax.text: Compression ratio estimates the algorithmic complexity of a genome—how much unique information it truly contains.

punchline.text: Compress the genome, find the real information. Repetition isn't complexity.

quiz.question: Why does the human genome compress so dramatically?
options: Massive repetitive and transposable elements create redundancy
